name: Question 17
problem: The geometric series $512+256+128⋯+16$  can be expressed using sigma notation as
worked_solution:
We must express the given series in the form

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{N}{a}_{1}{r}^{n-1},
$$

where ${a}_{1}$ denotes the first term of the series, $r$ denotes the common ratio, and $N$ denotes the number of terms in the series. In this case, ${a}_{1}=512.$

To find $r,$ we find the ratio of the consecutive terms ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}:$

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}}=\frac{256}{512}=\frac{1}{2}
$$

Now we must determine $N$ (the index of the last term). To do this, we use the fact that

$$
{a}_{N}={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{N-1}.
$$

Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{N-1} \\ 16 & =512\cdot {(\frac{1}{2})}^{N-1} \\ \frac{16}{512} & ={(\frac{1}{2})}^{N-1} \\ \frac{1}{32} & =\frac{1}{{2}^{N-1}} \\ 32 & ={2}^{N-1} \\ {2}^{5} & ={2}^{N-1} \\ 5 & =N-1 \\ N & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Expressing the geometric series in sigma notation, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}512+256+128⋯+16 & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{6}512\cdot {(\frac{1}{2})}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 17
?

The geometric series 512+256+128⋯+16 can be expressed using sigma notation as

a
∑n=17512⋅(12)n−1
b
∑n=16512⋅(12)n−1
c
∑n=16512⋅(13)n−1
d
∑n=15512⋅(12)n−1
e
∑n=17512⋅(13)n−1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We must express the given series in the form ∑n=1Na1rn−1,

where a1 denotes the first term of the series, r denotes the common ratio, and N denotes the number of terms in the series. In this case, a1=512.

To find r, we find the ratio of the consecutive terms a1 and a2: r=a2a1=256512=12

Now we must determine N (the index of the last term). To do this, we use the fact that aN=a1⋅rN−1.

Therefore aN=a1⋅rN−116=512⋅(12)N−116512=(12)N−1132=12N−132=2N−125=2N−15=N−1N=6.

Expressing the geometric series in sigma notation, we obtain:

512+256+128⋯+16=∑n=16512⋅(12)n−1
